answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a bond that is locked on-chain and slashable when an identity is caught double-claiming rewards or violating a signed rule. A newcomer may enter freely, but earning influence requires capital at risk and a track record that grows slowly; splitting into many identities multiplies the required bonds without multiplying trust. The lantern marks each account’s public history, while an oasis of cheap throwaway accounts cannot cross the canyon to costly influence without funds the attacker risks losing.
